toxicity.Notes: Acute oral toxicity by the OECD protocol: single gavage dose in a sunflower oil vehicle, six mice per complex, vehicle control, observation for 14 days with Hippocratic screening and no behavioural change reported. The animals had already been used for the oral bioavailability test and were reused on purpose. The protocol starts at 1000 mg/kg and adds 500 and 300 mg/kg when mortality exceeds 50 %, but only the 500 mg/kg series of complex 1 is shown, so no result is recorded for 300 mg/kg. Survival percentages are graph-read at day 14 from Fig. 2 and Fig. 3, where the step height matches six animals per group. Complex 2 caused no mortality at 1000 mg/kg, the highest dose tested, so the LD50 is recorded as a limit. The other two arms of the same experiment are not entered because the module takes only a named number: complex 1 killed all six mice at 1000 mg/kg and left 50 % alive at 500 mg/kg from day 2 to day 14, which the authors used to determine its LD50 without ever stating the value, and cisplatin given once at 500 mg/kg killed two of six mice. Treatment arm (column removed 2026-11-09): [Zn(atc-Ph)2], single oral dose, healthy mice. Cohort (column removed 2026-11-09): ijms17050781-acute-2. Group size basis (column removed 2026-11-09): cohort_all_assayed. Dose_basis (column removed 2026-11-16e): compound_mass. Source_locator (column removed 2026-11-16e): papers/10.3390_ijms17050781.pdf | Figs. 2 and 3; sections 2.4 and 3.11 | p. 6, p. 13.

pk.Analyte: Zn (ICP-OES, increment over the control baseline)
pk.Notes: Rapid oral bioavailability screen: single gavage dose of 300 mg/kg in female BALB/c mice, 4-8 weeks, 15-20 g, two animals per compound, blood from the retro-orbital veins at 20 min, 1, 2 and 4 h, plasma analysed for zinc by ICP-OES and for platinum by ICP-MS. Zinc values are given relative to the control sample because the body carries a baseline zinc level, so they are an increment over background and not a total plasma concentration; the detection limit for zinc was 480 ug/L. Reported series in ug/L: complex 1 2278.50, 3029.50, 1715.50, 935.55; complex 2 727.83, 1023.55, 1191.95, 624.70 at 20 min, 1, 2 and 4 h. Section 2.6 states in one sentence that the 20 min concentration of complex 1 was its Cmax, which contradicts its own series, the abstract and section 2.6 of the next page, all of which give 3029.50 ug/L at 1 h; the value at 1 h is entered and the contradiction kept here. No AUC, clearance, volume of distribution or half-life is reported, and with two animals per group no dispersion is given. Treatment arm (column removed 2026-11-09): [Zn(atc-Ph)2] 300 mg/kg single oral gavage. Cohort (column removed 2026-11-09): ijms17050781-pk-2.
